digest.headline: Ana Perić and Rosa Vidal talked at the harbor inn. Rosa Vidal: “You're the journalist everyone's talking about. I'm Rosa, I run this place. You need to hear things, you come here - I know what matters.” Ana Perić: “That's what I'm here for. What's the real story in Ferry Town, Rosa. What do people actually care about.” Rosa Vidal: “The mill's been shut for two months. Henrik who owned it just disappeared. People need work, they're scared. Nobody's talking about it openly but everyone feels it.” Ana Perić: “Henrik disappeared. That's something. Do you know where he went, or why he closed it.” Rosa Vidal: “Not yet. But there's money missing too, I hear. You sit here long enough, you'll learn the pieces. I can introduce you to people who know more than I do.”

items.text: Rosa Vidal arrived on the ferry.

Ana Perić and Luka Babić talked at the harbor. Ana Perić: “Morning. I'm Ana, I run the Gazette here. You look like you know the island. What brings you out in this weather?” Luka Babić: “Mill needs work. Roof's been bad since last winter.” Ana Perić: “The mill. So you're connected to that. Have people been talking about it needing repairs?” Luka Babić: “They talk. Nothing gets done.”

Luka Babić and Rosa Vidal talked at the harbor. Rosa Vidal: “You're Luka from the hill fields, aren't you. I've seen you at market. The mill roof - that's been on everyone's mind with the rain.” Luka Babić: “Mill needs work. The flour won't wait.” Rosa Vidal: “Petar came in this morning looking for suppliers. If you had grain ready, he'd take it. Might be worth a conversation at the inn.” Luka Babić: “The roof first. Then we'll see.”

items.text: Petar Ilić and Vesna Marić talked at the harbor inn. Petar Ilić: “You're Vesna, yeah? Heard you rent rooms. I need something longer than three nights at the inn, but I need to know the rates first.” Vesna Marić: “Fifty coins a week. Quiet place, no trouble. You look like someone who works early.” Petar Ilić: “I'm a baker. The rates are fair. But the room—does it stay at fifty, or does that change?” Vesna Marić: “Why would it change? You pay on time, it stays the same.” Petar Ilić: “Good. I'll let you know by tomorrow.”

items.text: Petar Ilić now thinks of Rosa Vidal: “Runs the inn, met me kindly, offered without me begging. Says she can help with the mill and suppliers. I was gruff with her and she didn't flinch. That counts.”
Vesna Marić now thinks of Petar Ilić: “Baker, direct, wants something more than three nights. No smell of trouble on him yet. Bakers keep hours, and people who keep hours pay on time.”

people.name: Ana Perić
people.opinion: Sharp, and she asks about Henrik and the mill like she already half knows. She gave me more than I gave her today, which either means she's generous or she's setting a hook. Either way I want her at my table.

people.name: Petar Ilić
people.opinion: Honest worry on him - a baker without flour has nowhere to hide it. He'll be back daily. First regular.

people.name: Ivana Horvat
people.opinion: Polite, careful, asking who decides things. That's not idle curiosity. I'll be warm and I'll watch what she writes down.
